# Intent: Safe Multi-Client MCP Setup

Disk Steward users can discover supported local AI clients, explicitly select one or more, and safely set up, verify, repair, or remove the read-only Disk Steward MCP integration without manually editing configuration files or confusing client setup with Agent Access.

## Success Evidence

- `REQ-401` — Settings detects supported installed clients through bounded known signals and lets the user select one or several targets without treating unknown software as supported.
- `REQ-402` — Setup, verification, repair, and removal are idempotent, preserve unrelated client configuration, refuse conflicting ownership, and provide recoverable evidence for every mutation.
- `REQ-403` — The UI distinguishes detection, configuration, client approval, verification, broken configuration, and Agent Access state with accessible text and per-client outcomes.
- `REQ-404` — Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Visual Studio Code, and Claude Desktop receive an honest supported setup path, while other MCP clients receive a copyable manual configuration rather than guessed mutation.
- `REQ-405` — The signed application bundle exposes a stable read-only helper path, and automated tests prove install, upgrade, conflict, verification, removal, and unrelated-setting preservation behavior.

## Constraints

- Preserve native Swift, macOS 13 compatibility, Homebrew and Developer ID distribution, and the bundled disk-witness-mcp helper.
- Use official client commands or client-owned installation flows when available; direct configuration editing is a bounded fallback only.
- Never require administrator privileges, store client credentials, enable Agent Access implicitly, or add write/delete MCP tools.
- Preserve unrelated client configuration and the completed crash-recovery intent and evidence.
- Keep detection bounded to known bundle identifiers, executables, and configuration locations; do not search the whole disk.

## Non-Goals

- Build a general MCP marketplace or gateway.
- Configure unrecognized clients automatically.
- Add remote MCP hosting, OAuth brokerage, or credential management.
- Redesign monitoring, evidence retention, or cleanup behavior.
- Grant agents destructive disk operations.

## Assumptions

- `ASM-401` (medium) — The distributed non-sandboxed app can invoke installed client CLIs and update user-owned configuration without additional entitlements.
- `ASM-402` (medium) — A helper path inside an app installed at a stable Applications location remains valid across normal Homebrew and in-place application updates.
